label: Mithraic Altar and Jemima's statue
more: Jemima and her husband Philip Yorke put up a flint 'Persian' altar, designed by her tutor Thomas Wright, with Greek inscription by Daniel Wray, as a learned garden joke. Her lead statue, reading a book, is dated about 1748 and probably by John Cheere.

label: Chinese Temple built
more: Jemima had a timber Chinese summerhouse built beside the new Broad Water, about 1760 (Chinese features in her garden date from the late 1750s). Historic England says William Chambers, designer of the Kew Pagoda, possibly designed it. Edward Stevens repaired it in 1769.

label: Ancient altars bought by Amabel
more: Amabel, Countess de Grey, bought five marble altars of the late second to first century BC from a Mr Beauclere of Muswell Hill and set them on a lawn. Where he found them is unknown.

label: Chinese Bridge rebuilt in brick
more: Anne Florence, Countess Cowper, designed a brick bridge with a single elliptical arch, built by estate workmen to replace a timber bridge of the 1760s. Date stones carry her monogram. The temple was rebuilt or remodelled for her the same year.
